new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Minor: the reader says Akeu 'appears once'; there is a second name-only mention the reader missed: 'Ake (阿克)' as a leaf of Southern Nisoic in Figure 2.5 'The Niso-Burmese and the Qiang-Rong under TB (Li 2010:44)', printed p. 49 (PDF p. 68). It is a reproduced classification tree with no data, so it says nothing about stress and does not change the reading. No silent-or-unopened works remained to spot-check beyond the single listed work; instead I re-verified the two supporting Hayashi quotes held by the project: Hayashi 2021 PDF p. 4 'Regarding the suprasegmentals, Menglun Akeu has a syllabic tonal system. sources.citation: Hayashi, Norihiko. 2021. Notes on the Phonological Development of Menglun Akeu. In Nagano Yasuhiko & Ikeda Takumi (eds.), Grammatical Phenomena of Sino-Tibetan Languages 4: Link Languages and Archetypes in Tibeto-Burman, 1-23. Kyoto: Institute for Research in Humanities, Kyoto University. hdl:2433/263976.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 4: 'Regarding the suprasegmentals, Menglun Akeu has a syllabic tonal system. There are three tonemes: 55, 33, and 21.' The only mention of stress (p. 16, fn. 28) concerns Youle Jino ('its stress pattern is usually iambic'), not Akeu. p. 21 fn. 32: Menglun Akeu and Akha Buli show very few examples of tone sandhi.

sources.citation: Hayashi, Norihiko (林范彦) & Gao Xiang (高翔). 2019. 中国云南省勐仑阿克语音系简介 [A Phonological Sketch of Menglun Akeu, Yunnan, China]. 神戸外大論叢 (Kobe Gaidai Ronso) 70(1): 37-66. Kobe City University of Foreign Studies. In Chinese.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (no 重音/轻声/stress/accent anywhere in the text layer). §4 声调 (p. 46): Menglun Akeu has three main tones 55, 33, 21, plus marginal 35 and 53 in a few words; syllable structure C1C2VC3/T with T = tone on every syllable; wordlist of ~600 items all tone-marked, no stress marks.
